title: Build the clinic database
instructions:
## The brief

A community clinic needs a database. Write a script that creates two tables and loads the first records. The database starts **empty**.

**patients**

| column | type | rules |
|---|---|---|
| id | INTEGER | primary key |
| name | TEXT | required |
| date_of_birth | TEXT | required (ISO date, e.g. 1998-04-17) |
| phone | TEXT | optional, but unique when given |

**visits**

| column | type | rules |
|---|---|---|
| id | INTEGER | primary key |
| patient_id | INTEGER | required, must refer to a patient |
| visit_date | TEXT | required |
| temperature_c | REAL | optional, but between 30 and 45 when given (CHECK) |
| notes | TEXT | optional |

Then insert these rows:

- patients: (1, 'Akosua Boateng', '1998-04-17', '0244000111'), (2, 'Yaw Mensah', '1975-11-02', NULL)
- visits: (1, 1, '2026-10-01', 37.2, 'Headache'), (2, 2, '2026-10-01', 38.9, 'Fever'), (3, 1, '2026-10-15', NULL, 'Follow-up')

## Checks

The checker reads your tables back, and then tries to insert bad rows: a visit for a patient who does not exist, a temperature of 70, and a patient with no name. A correct schema refuses all three. SQLite enforces foreign keys only after `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;` so put that line first.

config.schema: -- The clinic database starts empty: your script creates it.

hints: `name TEXT NOT NULL`, `phone TEXT UNIQUE` (UNIQUE allows several NULLs).
`patient_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES patients(id)` makes the link; `temperature_c REAL CHECK (temperature_c BETWEEN 30 AND 45)` limits the value.
`INSERT INTO patients VALUES (1, 'Akosua Boateng', '1998-04-17', '0244000111'), (2, 'Yaw Mensah', '1975-11-02', NULL);`

checks.label: Both tables exist with the right rows

probes.query: SELECT id, name, date_of_birth, phone FROM patients ORDER BY id
probes.name: the patients table

probes.query: SELECT id, patient_id, visit_date, temperature_c, notes FROM visits ORDER BY id
probes.name: the visits table

checks.label: A visit for a patient who does not exist is refused
checks.statement: PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON; INSERT INTO visits VALUES (4, 99, '2026-10-20', 37.0, 'x')
checks.message: The visits table accepted a patient_id that does not exist. Add REFERENCES patients(id) and keep PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON at the top.

checks.label: A temperature of 70 is refused
checks.message: The visits table accepted a temperature of 70. Add a CHECK constraint on temperature_c.

checks.label: A patient without a name is refused
checks.statement: INSERT INTO patients VALUES (3, NULL, '2000-01-01', NULL)
checks.message: The patients table accepted a NULL name. Add NOT NULL.

checks.label: Two patients cannot share a phone number
checks.message: Two patients were allowed the same phone number. Add UNIQUE to phone.

realityNote: PostgreSQL and MySQL enforce foreign keys by default and have real DATE types; SQLite stores dates as text, which is why the ISO format matters so sorting works.
